scope.future_policy: Use invented successor identities after the historical cutoff. Research informs institutions and political careers; it does not predict offices held by real people. Label fiction.
scope.claim: All five represented top-level parties have real 1990 leaders. The six UDF constituent streams are retained. This is a partial research staging file, not a complete France roster or finished avatar delivery.
scope.unrepresented_parties: Greens/EELV/Les Écologistes, MRG/PRG, LCR/NPA, LO, MDC/MRC, La France insoumise, Renaissance and other post-1990 formations need distinct game identities. UMP/LR and the multiple UDF successor organizations must not silently replace the 1990 rows.

ingestion.runtime_prerequisite: Do not import automatically. The runtime's generic party-to-executive mapping and the 11 UDF component slots need a deliberate role-aware integration and save-migration decision. A party chair, constituent executive, parliamentary leader and national executive must not become interchangeable. No runtime import or save migration is performed by this artifact.
ingestion.people: Compatible Person records; preserve existing Michel Rocard and François Mitterrand IDs, names and office_links when merging. François Mitterrand is not inserted as 1990 PS first secretary.
ingestion.parties: Compatible Party/Term fields only. Sources and research limitations remain explicit. UDF federation and components are distinct. Do not replace existing save-hash IDs.
ingestion.intervals: Half-open [from, until). Month/year bounds are uncertainty windows, not known vacancies. When a source lists a final inclusive day, normalize to the next day or successor start; election dates and assumption of office are distinguished.
ingestion.affiliations: Only evidenced office/coverage windows are supplied, not complete party membership. Open terms are verified only through reference_through.
ingestion.missing_life_dates: Unverified births/deaths are omitted; absence of died is not evidence of life at the current date.
ingestion.scope_clipping: Some constituent terms start at 1990-01-01 to describe the researched game period, not the actual date they first took office. Clipped windows are identified in term notes.

parties.identity_note: 1990 UDF was a federation of distinct political organizations. Its federal president is recorded alongside constituent executives, not as their replacement. The 1998 Nouvelle UDF reorganization merged some components while others remained associated or departed. MoDem, Nouveau Centre, UMP and later organizations are separate branches; this row is not assigned an invented single 2007–2026 successor chain.

lifecycle_notes.note: The President of the Republic and the PS first secretary are separate offices. Mitterrand's existing identity and office link must remain intact; Mauroy is the 1990 party leader. Acting and collective directions are distinct from elected first-secretary mandates.

The RPR's dissolution congress was September 21, 2002; this file includes that final calendar day and ends on September 22. The multi-party UMP merger and later LR name belong to a separately researched lineage, not an automatic continuation of this exact row.

UDF was a federation with six constituent streams at the 1990 start. Federal leadership, PR, CDS, Radical, PSD, club federation and direct members remain separately addressable. The PSD's documented general secretary is retained while Max Lejeune's formal/honorary presidency status is left unresolved.

Later Force démocrate, Démocratie libérale, PPDF and PRIL identities are distinct components. A component's period associated with UDF is not its entire existence or the leader's entire career. Force démocrate's Bayrou presidency ends in September 1998; its later November merger is a different event.

The 2007 transition generated multiple branches, including MoDem and Nouveau Centre. Bayrou's evidenced UDF presidency ends after November 30, 2007. Residual legal UDF, later name use and the independent successor organizations need separate lifecycle decisions; this file does not invent a unique chain through 2026.

Marchais's general-secretary title differs from Hue's and successors' national-secretary title. In 2001 Hue became president alongside Buffet as national secretary, so both offices are recorded. Hue's later presidency end remains coarse; no disappearance of Buffet's leadership is implied.

The FN became RN in June 2018. The 2017 acting appointments and Bardella's 2021 acting role are distinct from election as president in November 2022. Marine Le Pen's later parliamentary leadership does not make her the serving party president.

life_date_notes.note: LCP's June 1, 2026 obituary places death in the night spanning May 31/June 1 and birth in 1940. Year precision is deliberate; no invented exact birth or death day. A death record or family/municipal announcement can refine this.

source_quality.primary_sources: Official party histories and biographies; National Archives authority records; Senate and Assembly biographies; Élysée and government speech archives; HATVP office-holder disclosure; broadcaster footage for observed appearance.
source_quality.qualification: A public archive's biographical summary is an institutional source but is not always the original appointment instrument. Contemporary statements and congress records are preferred for exact office dates. Official sites can contain caption or timeline errors; conflicts are recorded rather than silently resolved.
source_quality.secondary_sources: France-politique.fr is Laurent de Boissieu's specialist chronology, not an official party or government source. Le Monde, AFP reports carried by La Dépêche, RFI, RTL, Europe 1, L'Orient-Le Jour and LCP reporting are identified as secondary/contemporary reporting where used; quoted first-person announcements provide corroboration but are not original minutes.
source_quality.precision: The dataset deliberately preserves month/year precision and marked observation windows when exact appointment dates have not been established. The research is partial, not certified complete.
